text:
Maya (Support): Heads-up — customer ACME filing an escalated ticket. They say streamed responses sometimes cut out mid-response and were billed for the entire token batch. They pasted this snippet from their client: `write: broken pipe`. They want rollback/credit and a root cause.

Alex (SRE): Can you paste the full request id / headers from the customer? Need X-Request-ID + gateway logs. Also, are they on our hosted API or Dedicated?

Maya (Support): Hosted. X-Request-ID: rQ-7f3d2c1a. Customer reported it happens about 1-2% of streams during peak. Their curl snippet:
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" \
  -H "Transfer-Encoding: chunked" \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate?model=redwood-alpha -d @- <<'PAYLOAD'
{"prompt":"long prompt...","max_tokens":1200}
PAYLOAD
```
Then they hit ctrl-c after ~8s and sometimes still get billed for tokens produced after the ctrl-c.

Priya (Eng - Runtime): I pulled rQ-7f3d2c1a from gateway logs and runtime traces. Sequence:
1) gateway accepted request and proxied to runtime via envoy
2) runtime started streaming chunks
3) midway we see `write tcp 10.10.4.23:443->172.20.30.44:51234: write: broken pipe` in the runtime stdout
4) envoy emitted `upstream premature response: reset` and returned 502 to the client
5) billing pipeline currently reads the final HTTP code (502) and marks it as a 5xx chargeable failure for accounting
Logs:
```
[2026-03-14T14:12:05Z] runtime: stream write -> chunk_len=482
[2026-03-14T14:12:10Z] runtime: write error: broken pipe (syscall write)
[2026-03-14T14:12:10Z] envoy: upstream reset, rst_type=connection_failure
[2026-03-14T14:12:10Z] gateway: responded 502 to client, trace=rQ-7f3d2c1a
```

Alex (SRE): OK that confirms server encountered a write error after the client closed its read side. We need to distinguish: server-initiated 5xx vs client abort. If the TPROXY/envoy chain returns 502 because upstream closed while writing, our billing heuristic shouldn't automatically treat as revenue-eligible 5xx — sometimes it's the client who disconnected early.

Sam (Billing): We've already had one charge dispute from ACME for $12.40. At present the billing service groups by final HTTP code + token_count. If it's a client abort, we should credit. Do we have token-level logs to prove what was actually delivered to the client vs produced by runtime?

Priya (Eng - Runtime): Token emission is logged at the runtime level but not reliably correlated with socket write success. We log `emitted_token:N` when generated and `write_chunk:ok` when socket write returns ok. In this failure trace we have emitted_token logs for tokens 1..420 and then write error on chunk that included tokens 421..482 — the socket write returned an error. Practically the client only received tokens up to 420.
```
emitted_token: 418
emitted_token: 419
emitted_token: 420
write_chunk: failed err="write: broken pipe" chunk_id=37 tokens=62
```

Maya (Support): Customer asserts they disconnected at token 420 and shouldn't be billed for 421+. They have diagnostic traces showing their client aborted. They want a credit. I've already offered temporary credit while we investigate. Putting this thread on P2 escalation.

Alex (SRE): Short term mitigation ideas:
- Add fast rule in billing to treat 502/5xx with runtime write errors (errno EPIPE/ECONNRESET) as ‘client abort’ candidate until proven otherwise. That would auto-flag for manual review instead of immediate charge.
- Emit a `socket_write_success` audit event with token_range for every stream so billing can precisely bill only up to last-successful-token.

Sam (Billing): We can add an override flag for credits, but we need a deterministic mapping so ops doesn't get flooded. If runtime emits `write_chunk:failed` we can treat that request as `client_disconnected` and zero-bill the final incomplete tokens. Need runtime change to write success/fail events to the audit bus.

Priya (Eng - Runtime): I'll open a quick PR to emit `socket_write_result` events to our kafka audit topic within the same transaction as token emission. That will let billing reconstruct delivered token counts. PR will include schema:
```json
{"type":"socket_write_result","trace":"rQ-...","chunk_id":37,"tokens_attempted":62,"success":false,"err":"EPIPE"}
```
```
(note: in JSON event above, we'll keep values small strings/ints for backward compatibility)
```

Doug (PM): Timeline/impact? Customers keep disputing charges. Would prefer a fast mitigation that doesn't require a full runtime roll to prod. Can we do a billing-side heuristic first?

Alex (SRE): Yes — short-term: add billing-side heuristic to treat 5xx where the runtime reported `write_chunk:failed` or envoy reported `upstream reset` within 1s of the last emitted token as a candidate to credit. Medium-term: runtime event and a small runtime release to guarantee write success events. Longer-term: move token-level metering to proxy layer (gateway) so billing sees what was actually sent on the wire.

deploy-bot: Deployment event: gateway v2.4.1 rolled to us-east-1 at 2026-03-14T15:00:00Z. No related rollout failures reported. (reaction :white_check_mark:)

Maya (Support): For ACME I've created interim credit for the disputed $12.40 and let them know we're applying a heuristic. They want a postmortem + action. Can we provide ETA?

Priya (Eng - Runtime): I'll open PR by EOD with the audit event instrumentation and a tiny consumer change for the billing staging pipeline. If tests pass we can ship to staging in 48h and prod in ~7 days if no issues.

Sam (Billing): I'll implement the heuristic in the billing service to consult the `write_chunk:failed` audit topic and flag candidate requests for auto-credit. I'll also add a dashboard showing number of requests flagged vs credited so we can monitor churn.

Alex (SRE): I'll add logs/metrics: `runtime.write_errors_total{err="EPIPE"}`, `billing.flagged_for_client_abort_total`. Also correlate with `stream_latency_p95` to see if heavier loads correlate.

Doug (PM): Good. Owner roll-up:
- Priya: runtime audit events PR + staging rollout (ETA 48h)
- Sam: billing heuristic + dashboard (ETA 72h)
- Alex: metrics + alert if flagged>1% (ETA 24h)
- Maya: customer comms / credit issued (done)

Maya (Support): Thanks all. I put the ticket owner as Priya and linked this thread to ACME ticket #INC-2145. I'll follow up with the customer after the staging rollout.

Priya (Eng - Runtime): Quick repro notes for the eng team (recording here so support can reference):
Steps to reproduce locally:
1) Start a simple streaming client that reads chunks and then kills the TCP connection mid-stream (simulate ctrl-c). E.g. `curl` + `tcpkill` or `nc` and then `kill -9` on client PID.
2) Observe runtime `write: broken pipe` and envoy upstream reset.
3) Confirm billing pipeline currently records final HTTP 502 and counts tokens produced rather than tokens delivered.
Example tcpkill command (dev only):
```bash
# start the curl streaming in terminal A
# in terminal B (requires sudo):
sudo tcpkill -i lo port 443 and host <client-ip>
```

Alex (SRE): One more note: dont rely on `tcpkill` in production. For controlled testing use a test client that issues FIN properly or sends RST to emulate client abort. `tcpkill` can be noisy in multi-tenant dev boxes.

Sam (Billing): I'll queue a retroactive script to reconcile the last 48h of flagged requests and auto-create credits where the runtime event shows `success=false` for the final chunk. Will need sign-off from finance for credits > $500/day. I'll report counts tomorrow.

Maya (Support): Closing note: customer appreciative of quick credit. Marking thread resolved for support ops, keep engineering owners in loop until prod instrumentation + billing rule shipped. :thumbsup:
